result.topic_en: Euler recalls how isoperimetric problems, where one integral is extremized among curves sharing the values of other integrals, were once thought very hard, and notes that his treatise reduced them to the simple unconstrained extremization of a combined integral with multipliers.
result.transcription:
70 METH. NOVA CALCVL. VARIAT. TRACT.

55. Cum olim haec Methodus maximorum et minimorum tractari eſt coepta, non ſolum eiusmodi curuae ſunt inueſtigatae in quibus formula quaepiam integralis $\int Z\,dx$ eſſet vel maximum vel minimum; ſed etiam eiusmodi quaeſtiones proponebantur, vt non inter omnes plane curuas, ſed inter eas tantum, quae habeant eandem longitudinem ea quaeratur, in qua illa formula fiat maxima vel minima, ex quo ipſo caſu nomen Problematis Iſoperimetrici eſt natum hoc autem nomen non impediuit, quo minus eiusmodi quaeſtiones generaliores proponerentur, vt inter omnes eas curuas quibus valor certae cuiuspiam formulae integralis $\int V\,dx$ aeque conueniat, ea definiatur in qua formula $\int Z\,dx$ maximum minimumve ſortiatur valorem; quin etiam conditiones adhuc fuerunt multiplicatae in hunc modum, vt tantum inter omnes eas curuas, quibus non ſolum formula $\int V\,dx$, ſed etiam hae quotcunque $\int V'\,dx$, $\int V''\,dx$ etc. aequaliter competant, ea definiatur in qua $\int Z\,dx$ ſit maximum vel minimum, cuiusmodi problemata tum temporis ſummopere ardua ſunt viſa. Poſtquam vero in tractatu meo de hoc argumento oſtendiſſem huiusmodi problemata ſemper reduci poſſe ad hoc problema ſimplex, quo inter omnes plane lineas, ea inueſtigetur, in qua haec formula integralis
$$\int dx\,(Z + \alpha V + \beta V' + \gamma V'' \text{ etc.})$$
fiat maximum vel minimum, huius generis problemata nullam amplius habent difficultatem.

DE

items.quote: Poſtquam vero in tractatu meo de hoc argumento oſtendiſſem huiusmodi problemata ſemper reduci poſſe ad hoc problema ſimplex, quo inter omnes plane lineas, ea inueſtigetur, in qua haec formula integralis $$\int dx\,(Z + \alpha V + \beta V' + \gamma V'' \text{ etc.})$$ fiat maximum vel minimum, huius generis problemata nullam amplius habent difficultatem.
items.english: But after I had shown in my treatise on this subject that problems of this kind can always be reduced to this simple problem, in which, among absolutely all lines, the one is sought in which this integral formula $\int dx\,(Z + \alpha V + \beta V' + \gamma V'' \text{ etc.})$ becomes a maximum or minimum, problems of this type no longer present any difficulty.

items.quote: vt inter omnes eas curuas quibus valor certae cuiuspiam formulae integralis $\int V\,dx$ aeque conueniat, ea definiatur in qua formula $\int Z\,dx$ maximum minimumve ſortiatur valorem
items.english: that among all curves to which the value of some given integral formula $\int V\,dx$ belongs equally, the one be determined in which the formula $\int Z\,dx$ obtains a maximum or minimum value
